qa.question: Is each MTU engine at ELN03 rated 3,490 kilowatts or 3,250 kilowatts?
qa.finding: The permit table at https://deq.nd.gov/AQ/Notices/AppliedDigital/DRAFT_ACP18338v1_0.pdf says the 48 MTU 20V4000 DS3250 engines produce 3,490 kilowatts each. The analysis at https://deq.nd.gov/AQ/Notices/AppliedDigital/DRAFT_ACP18338v1_0AQEA.pdf says 3,250 kilowatts each. The database uses 3.49 megawatts per engine and 167.52 megawatts in total.
qa.recommendation: Keep 3.49 for now. Ask the North Dakota air quality office which figure the final permit uses, and change to 3.25 and 156.0 megawatts if it says 3,250.
qa.note: The commission filing at https://www.psc.nd.gov/webdocs/case/26-0155/001-010.pdf says the site plans about 252 engines of 3 megawatts each, up to 756 megawatts. That rounds the MTU engines down and does not settle the question.

qa.question: Should the Ellendale plant point move to the permit address?
qa.finding: The permit at https://deq.nd.gov/AQ/Notices/AppliedDigital/DRAFT_ACP18338v1_0.pdf gives 9663 87th Ave. SE, Ellendale. The geocoded point is 46.01096, -98.56866, which is 1.3 kilometers from the database point.
qa.recommendation: Move the plant to the new point and keep it approximate. Check the data center location in current imagery before calling it exact.
qa.note: Imagery was of unknown date and showed no data center buildings, so the buildings could not be seen.
